about: The production-readiness scorecard launch-readiness grades and readiness-score.py evaluates. Levels are cumulative gates, never weighted sums. Extend by ADDING rules (Track B Phase 7 adds rows); never rename an id or add a field a rule must carry. Evidence kinds: file and doc-field are evaluated by the script; ledger, tool and runtime results are read only from the evidence TSV written in the same run.

rules.pass: an owners file covers every path of the feature (repo scope: at least one rule) with a human or team owner, not a bot only
rules.why: nobody is paged and nobody decides when the feature has no owner

rules.pass: the success file's fields are filled and typed; a template placeholder is FAIL
rules.why: a launch nobody can judge gets declared a success

rules.pass: the metric and counter-metric events are fired (no AN §2 row for them); a recorded query returning NO-DATA or STALE is FAIL
rules.why: a metric with no data cannot judge the launch

rules.pass: no finding at medium or above on the feature's paths
rules.why: a risky path with no switch cannot be stopped without a deploy

rules.pass: no finding at medium or above for error, empty, loading and permission states on the feature's screens
rules.why: the first failed request shows a blank screen or a spinner forever

rules.pass: no unserved call and no shipped placeholder on the feature's routes
rules.why: the first real user meets a 404 or fake rows

rules.pass: no open BLOCKER or HIGH security finding on the feature's paths
rules.why: a known exploitable defect ships with the launch

rules.pass: a rollback record (environment, ISO time, result) and the irreversible emissions, or none
rules.why: code reverts; data written and notifications sent do not

rules.pass: the decision rule is written with a threshold, a named owner and a future review date
rules.why: a threshold chosen after the result is chosen to justify it

rules.pass: every fatal x high assumption is tested or accepted by a named person (repo scope: every one past its expiry)
rules.why: the bet nobody tested becomes a fact by default

rules.pass: the feature's endpoints are covered by alerts that carry a resolving runbook link
rules.why: an alert with no runbook pages a person who cannot act

rules.pass: readiness and health checks report the dependencies the feature needs, truthfully
rules.why: a probe that always answers 200 routes traffic to a broken instance

rules.pass: every shipped locale holds every key the feature renders (N/A with a reason for a single-locale product)
rules.why: a missing key renders a raw key or the wrong language

rules.pass: no finding at medium or above (N/A with a reason when the product has no plans)
rules.why: the pricing page promises what the gate refuses, or gives away what was sold

rules.pass: every acceptance criterion id of the feature is named by a test that asserts it
rules.why: an untested promise is found by the first user, not the suite

rules.pass: a release note describes the change for the people who will receive the questions
rules.why: support learns about the change from the first confused customer

rules.pass: every user journey the feature touches has an ai/runtime/slos.md row with SLI, target, window, a named owner and an origin
rules.why: with no stated objective nobody can say the feature is degraded, and no release step can be judged against it

rules.pass: every page-severity alert for the feature's services routes to a receiver that reaches the on-call rotation
rules.why: a page that lands in a null receiver or a muted channel is an outage nobody is told about

evidence.detector: /alert-design actionability ledger: 0 ORPHAN rows (each runbook path opened, not only linked as alert-rule-lint §2 checks)

rules.pass: every alert that can page for the feature has a runbook file that exists and names a concrete first action
rules.why: a runbook link to a missing file or to 'investigate' is relearned at 3 a.m. every time

rules.pass: every outbound call on the feature's request path has a timeout and a total deadline
rules.why: one slow dependency with no timeout holds every worker and takes the feature down with it

rules.pass: the feature's migrations are expand-only for the running release and reversible, or carry a recovery point; N/A with the reason when none ship
rules.why: a contract step in the same release makes rollback impossible: the old code reads a schema that is gone

rules.pass: the feature's user journey has an SLO as code with burn-rate alerts
rules.why: without an SLO nobody can say the feature is degraded until users say so

rules.pass: a load-test script exists for the feature's hot endpoints and a recorded run met its budget
rules.why: the launch spike is the first load test otherwise

evidence.external: a measured restore (dr-audit or a drill record)

rules.pass: a restore of the feature's data was measured against its RTO
rules.why: an untested backup is a hypothesis

rules.pass: the rollout is progressive with a real analysis gate
rules.why: a rollout with no analysis gate promotes a regression to everyone

rules.pass: the feature's conversion events fire on the confirmed outcome
rules.why: attempts counted as conversions inflate the result the launch is judged by

rules.pass: a rollback to a ledgered GREEN revision resolved, passed the reversibility gate R1-R3 and was rehearsed in staging
rules.why: a rollback that was never exercised fails the night it is needed: a reaped image, a mutable tag, a contract migration

rules.owner: performance/load-test (breakpoint or stress run) + saturation metrics

evidence.external: a measured capacity headroom (breakpoint or stress run, or saturation at the observed peak)

rules.pass: the projected launch peak sits below the measured breaking point with the headroom the owner set, read on the saturating resource
rules.why: without measured headroom the first traffic spike finds the limit in production

rules.pass: an error-budget policy says what happens when the feature's SLO budget is spent, and who signs
rules.why: a spent budget with no policy changes nothing: releases continue into the outage
